Author: J.K. Maheshwari
Bench: J.K. Maheshwari
 In The Supreme Court Of India
 Civil/Criminal Original Jurisdiction
 Transfer Petition (Civil) No. 1008 Of 2021
 Chetna Chopra Petitioner(s)
 Versus
 Iqbal Singh Mann Respondent(s)
 With
 Transfer Petition (Criminal) No. 232 Of 2021
 O R D E R
These transfer petitions have been filed by the petitioner(wife) against the husband and mother-in- law seeking transfer of the cases, as prayed, in the said petitions.
As directed by this Court on 30.08.2022, parties were referred to the Delhi High Court Mediation and Conciliation Centre to mediate the issues and, if possible, arrive at an amicable settlement.

entities.text: Delhi High Court Mediation and Conciliation Centre
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: After having talks at mediation, on 18.07.2023, the respondent gave a proposal to which a counter other side, as directed on 25.07.2023.
After deliberations, a joint application being Interlocutory Application No. 157196 of 2023 has been filed along with Settlement Deed dated 08.08.2023 duly signed by the parties.

In terms of the said Settlement Deed, the parties have agreed on the following terms:
Now, the parties to the present Settlement Deed, have amicably settled all their disputes and have agreed to settle the matter as per the following terms and conditions:-
1. That the Second Party has agreed to pay a sum of Rs.50,00,000/-(Fifty Lakhs only)
towards the marriage and higher education expenses (i.e. Rs.25 Lakhs each under both head) of the minor daughter, which shall be paid in the shape of Fixed Deposits in the following manner: -

1  S. No. Amount of FDR Date (on or  before)
 1. Rs.15,00,000/- 30.09.2023  2. Rs.15,00,000/- 31.12.2023

entities.text: Chetna Chopra vs Iqbal Singh Mann
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: That the aforesaid FDRs shall be in the name of the minor child i.e. Inaaya Kaur Mann and the FDRs at S. No. 1 and 3 shall be for a tenure of 14 years each and are meant to be utilized for the purpose of higher education.
The FDRs at S.No. 2 and 4 are towards her marriage expenses and shall be for a tenure of 18 years each.
The First Party shall provide all the documents to the second party which may be required for the purpose of FDRs by the bank in this regard.

3. The the Second Party shall further pay a monthly amount of Rs.20,000/- by 07th of every English Calender month towards educational expenses/maintenance of the minor daughter till she clears her school education (upto Class XII).
The above said amount will be transferred directly in the existing Bank Account of the minor daughter (i.e. Account No. 922010002436335 in Axis Bank, New Delhi).

The agreed payment shall be made by the Second Party in the said Bank Account commencing from the month of Sep.
2023.

4. The parties acknowledge that after execution of the present Settlement Deed, there shall remain no claim or cause of action against each other or any of their family members on any account whatsoever.

The aforesaid terms and condition would include and cover all claims, maintenance,
arrears, alimony, or any amount under other head whatsoever, of the First Party and the daughter of the parties against the Second Party and/or his family members.

5. The First Party shall have the custody of the daughter and the Second Party will have visitation rights towards the minor daughter on every alternate weekends (Saturday or Sunday), when the Second Party shall be permitted to meet the child from 12 noon to 4 pm at a place as mutually decided by the First and Second Party.
The said visitations should not be in conflict with extra circular activities of the child.
Both the parties undertake not to pollute the mind of the child and spoil her with unnecessary gifts.

In case of any trips, both parties shall give prior information to the other party with respect to the location and itinerary, etc.
6.

That it is further agreed that the Second Party shall be entitled to have visitation rights of the minor daughter to celebrate (a) festivals for one day each (5-6 hours) before the festival of Holi, Diwali, Christmas and New Year,
(b) Birthday of Second Party for one day (for 5-6 hours).
The First Party shall also have a right to accompany the child during all these visits, to the residence to Second Party.

Chetna Chopra vs Iqbal Singh Mann on 11 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71704584/
2 7.

entities.text: Chetna Chopra vs Iqbal Singh Mann
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Second Party shall also be entitled to accompany the First Party to visit the minor daughters school/college and attend parent teacher meetings, annual day, sports day or any other events and functioning of the school and interact with the minor daughter in school premises.

The name,
address and phone number of the Second Party shall be made available in the records of the school/college attended by the minor daughter.

Further, the Second Party can guide his daughter as regards to her education including but not limited to choosing her graduation/ post-graduation college/ university/ stream and can accompany the First party to visit the college/university for admission or any other purposes/events in college/university.
The First Party shall also permit the minor daughter to communicate with the Second Party through video-conferencing/mobile as per mutual discussions.
8. That on attaining the age of maturity, the minor daughter shall be permitted to stay overnight with the Second Party for such duration, as she wishes.

In case of remarriage of the Second Party,
overnight stay and visit to Second partys house will cease and monthly (alternate weekends)
visitations can continue.
9. The Second Party shall return the passport of the child to the mother i.e. the First Party before the Honble Supreme Court.
The Second Party shall also co- operate with the first party to do needful for renewal of child passport.
Both the parties shall co-operate with each other in all the documentations which may be required from time to time by the minor child.

10. That the Second Party shall be entitled to attend and perform all the rituals of a father at the time of marriage and other functions (engagement, etc.) of the minor daughter. The Second Party shall also be allowed to invite his friends (2) and Sisters (2) and their family members except the spouse and kids from the re-marriage, if any, of the Second Party to attend such functions.
11. The Second Party and his parents are most welcome to celebrate the childs birthday by either planning or attending and celebrating her birthday party along with the First party.
Both the parents can mutually decide ways to celebrate the childs birthday keeping in mind her wish as well.
12. Keeping in mind the health situation of the child, the second party is entitled to attend her health checkups related to her Kidney and interact with the doctors.

He can be in touch with the First party to inquire the general well-being of the child and both the parties to coordinate and plan the doctor visit for regular check-ups, tests or scans, etc.
13.

That the parties have agreed to obtain divorce by mutual consent and a joint application in this regard will be moved before the Honble Supreme Court under Article 142 of the Constitution of India and if so required, before the competent Court.
The parties shall co-operate with each other in obtaining divorce by mutual consent.

14. That in view of the present settlement, the First Party shall have no objection if the FIR No.
82/2023, PS Paschim Vihar East is quashed by this Honble Court or by Honble High Court, as the case may be.
The First Party undertakes to co-operate with the Second Party, in getting the aforesaid FIR quashed.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: That the parties undertake to withdraw all the cases, litigations, complaint filed by them or their family members against each other or their family members, before any Court or any other authority including FIR and complaints registered by both the parties.

16. That the terms and conditions as contained in the present Settlement Deed shall be binding upon both the parties and they undertake not to indulge in any kind of litigation against each other or their family members, with respect to the present marriage or on any other issue, in future.

In view of the terms of the said settlement, the following prayers were made:
It is most respectfully submitted that this Honble Court may kindly be pleased to : -
A) Pass appropriate directions to dissolve the marriage of the petitioner by passing a decree of divorce by mutual consent,

B) Quash the FIR No. 82/2023, PS Paschim Vihar East, Delhi u/s 498A/406/34 IPC.
C) Pass such other or further order(s) as this Honble Court deems fit and proper, in the facts and circumstances of the case.

We have heard Mr. Ravinder Singh, learned counsel for the petitioner along with Ms. Chetna Chopra, petitioner present in the Court in-person and also Mr. Sudhir Naagar, learned counsel for the respondent along with Mr. Iqbal Singh Mann, respondent present in the Court in-person.

Both have voluntarily stated that in terms of the Settlement Deed, decree of divorce by mutual consent may be directed by this Court in exercise of power under Article 142 of the Constitution of India, as the reunion is not desirable and possible between the parties.

Considering the aforesaid, we dispose of these transfer petitions in the following terms:
(1) We grant a decree of divorce to the petitioner (wife)-Ms.Chetna Chopra and the respondent(husband)-Mr.Iqbal Singh Mann in exercise of our powers under Article 142 of the Constitution of India.
Their marriage shall stand dissolved forthwith.

(2)
The respondent shall abide by the terms and conditions as specified in the Settlement Deed with respect to deposit of amounts specified in the table strictly observing the dates as specified.
The second party undertakes to this Court that he will strictly comply with the deposits on the dates as specified.
(3) Parties undertake to this Court that they shall abide by all the aforementioned terms and conditions as agreed by them in the Settlement Deed including the visitation rights as specified therein.
(4) Parties shall take steps to withdraw the cases filed against each other and culminate those proceedings within a period of four weeks from today.

On submitting a copy of the order, the said case shall be consigned to record.
Accordingly, these transfer petitions stand disposed of.
Pending application, if any, shall stand disposed of.
